Aquí te detallamos las razones principales:

Dificultad en la Detección Automática: Es difícil para un algoritmo diferenciar entre un jugador que está teniendo una "mala racha" o es de menor nivel, y uno que está perdiendo intencionalmente pero sin morir descaradamente (ej. farmear en lugar de pelear por objetivos).

Riesgo de Falsos Positivos: Sancionar de forma automática a jugadores que simplemente juegan mal (o tienen un mal día) puede frustrar a la base de jugadores legítimos. Riot prefiere la precaución antes de banear masivamente a usuarios inocentes.

Evolución del Troll: Los "trolls" han evolucionado; ya no solo mueren intencionalmente (hard inting), sino que venden objetos al final, siguen al jungla para robar campamentos o se quedan AFK moviéndose en base para evitar el sistema automático.

El Gray Area (Zona Gris): Acciones como no agruparse, forzar un "split push" o elegir campeones no convencionales (off-meta) son difíciles de penalizar porque, técnicamente, podrían estar intentando ganar de una forma distinta.

Katarina prays to Lillia like a temple deity, and in the end, the blessing allows them to reunite and make the plum blossom whole again.

It felt like a story about loss, memory, and reunion under divine grace.

Not gonna lie, I actually am pleasantly surprised at the risks Riot is taking for this new season regarding the role quests. There's obviously going to be *an absurd* amount of balancing required and headwinds in ensuring no one role is completely roflstomping the others. BUT, what matters is that they're taking risks with the game again. Seasons 13 and 14 were marred by very conservative changes that didn't make the game feel new and exciting really, it just felt like the same thing but with something else added to it (cough cough Atakhan). This time they're literally breaking the rules of the game with stuff like ADCs being allowed to buy 6 completed items, or top laners getting increased level cap. While it may sound crazy and power creepy, I think it's exactly the kind fo new stuff League needs to feel "new" again.

Anyway, here is my take on the theme (c/c from my tumblr because I am lazy), even though I lack proper technical knowledge in music. 

Arabic lyrics: 

Oh, knight, you are not a sinner. 
The sins of this world aren't yours to bear alone.

[The chorus is hard to get]

Oh, knight, you are not a sinner, you are not a sinner.

The track opens softly, with a violin elevating itself gently above the other strings before pinch strings take over and the lyrics start. In the first 30 seconds, we are left with a luminous impression that is tempered quickly by a somber, yet still gentle tone, leading us into lyrics that feel both like a lament and a reassurance. Indeed, Orkidian confirmed that Zaahen feels responsible for the Ascended/Darkins immortality, and I express my own theory that he was potentially a Sun Priest potentially leading the Ascension ritual - his design as a human/Ascended and his lines about how mortals should not meddle with the power of gods hint at something along that line. The use of religious imagery with the idea of not being a sinner and not bearing the sins of the world alone also supports that theory.

 The somber tone of the track remains with a soft string ensemble up until the 1:30 mark. During that part, I can really picture the sun-baked golden sands of Shurima and Zaahen's mindscape while he is sealed, his thoughts concerned but not overwhelmed. 

Then, the violin comes back, raising above the rest with that luminous tone as distorted drums start, the threat of corruption lapping at the edge of Zaahen's mind. He could let the corruption take over, but refuses the very idea, and will stand against himself as the Darkin urges emerge from within in an electric riff. The violin gets the upper hands, followed by the string ensemble with the drums and electric riffs still in the back, playing against the strings, to express Zaahen's steady determination. 

What could have been a dramatic turn becomes heroic instead, with Zaahen raising above what he could be, wrestling this inner darkness with each step he takes. 

By the 2:58 mark, the vocals are back, sounding almost like a prayer and a resolution as the tension remains steady. Then, by 3:37, the tension drops, and only the vocals and single violin remain, still singing "Oh knight, you are not a sinner, you are not a sinner". 

There's hints of Xin Zhao's theme peppered in there as well, supporting Zaahen's determination and driven noble character, just like he acknowledged Xin Zhao in his mindspace and accepted his sacrifice, understanding the similarities they have. 

I maintain the appreciation for the cinematic/historical fresco impression left by Zaahen's theme. Riot's Music department never disappoints, but this one truly is a memorable masterpiece. It's already one of my favourite champion themes, and I am glad a character like Zaahen gets to have such an epic theme. The whole creative process behind this character is delightfully well driven from start to finish.

I was genuinely touched, all three girls did wonderfully and delivered an incredibly impressive Finals opening ceremony

Edited: I was informed that Chrissy was sick in 2017. I am glad that Riot invited her to perform this year, for the game's 15th anniversary. It’s interesting because, as the child of immigrants growing up in the West, I see a part of myself in Xin Zhao’s story. Being born into one culture and then adopting another. For me, living in France, being French has nothing to do with origins—it’s about the connection you build with the culture, the history, and the foundations of the nation. Of course, it’s not always easy, since France also carries a colonial and slave-trade past (which somehow echoes Demacia’s prejudice against mages). WASD control for adc kiting is obviously a huge problem, but also I dont hear enough people talking about how it'll nerf skill shot reliant charcters super hard. There is a big aspect to dodging skill shots that people dont talk about, and that is after you see a skillshot incoming, you have your reaction time before you act on it, but then ALSO have the amount of time it takes to move your mouse from whatever position it was in to whatever position it needs to go to for dodging. Especially for low elo players who click far from their character, this is a non-negligible amount of time that WASD players will no longer have. Its also used a lot in trading (shooting skill shots at players when they are in actions. This works well because 1) they are in animation, and 2) their mouse is occupied pointing and clicking on their action, rather than in the direction they wish to dodge already.) WASD will make players exceptionally slippery compared to click to move players

This is really cool. At first Noxus seemed like a stand-in for the generic bad guy dark empire trope, which it still does. With lots of similarities with the Roman Empire, especially with gladiator arenas and the red color scheme. But now that Riot has expanded the lore on Mordekaiser and shown Noxus's bloody humble origins, it makes a lot more sense that Noxus's culture, values, and governance are a lot more Mongolian Empire. 1. This trailer is for the game's first 2025 competitive season because it has a Noxian theme
2. This cinematic was created by the same animators as the Arcane series, but it is just for the game
3. The next Arcane series is confirmed to be in Noxus, which is why they have Mel and Black Rose here and keep consistent to the lore and styles of the series, but there is no official release date yet

Maria Egan from Riot Games said about working with the band: ''What happens with Arcane is that we shall get sent some rough storyboards and there will be a temp track attached, it was a song that immediately made me think that Tyler Joseph has to write this. The moment was designed for this band and we knew that Tyler was a fan of the show and that they wanted to do something with us. He never really writes for anything else, but he loves the show so they wanted to see it and we sent it over. Literally three days after he got the scene, we got the song back, when that one came in it was like, ‘Okay, well, that’s it’. We were able to work really closely with them to create this moment. He’ll tell his own story about it, but he has his own investment in what the song means to him. But he really loves the show so he was so into being part of the world and trying to tell the story. He’s an exceptional songwriter, and he’s always been one of my favourite writers, lyrically. That’s a very masterful skill; to take specific stories and make them universal. There’s a handful of writers at any given time on the planet that do that well, and Tyler’s definitely one of them.”

Grass is a plant with narrow leaves growing from the base. A common kind of grass is used to cover the ground in a lawn and other places. Grass gets water from the roots in the ground. Grass is usually pigmented with the colour ‘green’. Grasses are monocotyledon, herbaceous plants. The grasses include the "grass", of the family Poaceae (also called Gramineae). Also sometimes it is used to include the sedges (Cyperaceae) and the rushes (Juncaceae). These three families are not closely related but belong to different clades in the order Poales. They are similar adaptations to a common life-style. The true grasses include cereals, bamboo and the grasses of lawns (turf) and grassland. Uses for graminoids include food (as grain, sprouted grain, shoots or rhizomes), drink (beer, whisky), pasture for livestock, thatching thatch, paper, fuel, clothing, insulation, construction, sports turf, basket weaving and many others. Many grasses are short, but some grasses, like bamboo can grow very tall. Plants from the grass family can grow in many places, even if they are very cold or very dry. Several other plants that look similar but are not members of the grass family are also sometimes called grass; these include rushes, reeds, papyrus, and water chestnut. Grasses are an important food for many animals, like deer, buffalo, cattle, mice, grasshoppers, caterpillars, and many other grazers. Unlike other plants, grasses grow from the bottom, so when animals eat grass they usually do not destroy the part that grows. Without grass, dirt can wash away into rivers (erosion). Graminoids include some of the most versatile plant life-forms. They became widespread toward the end of the Cretaceous. Fossilized dinosaur dung (coprolites) have been found containing grass phytoliths (silica stones inside grass leaves). Grasses have adapted to conditions in lush rain forests, dry deserts, cold mountains and even intertidal habitats, and are now the most widespread plant type. Grass is a valuable source of food and energy for many animals.Lawn grass is often planted on sports fields and in the area around a building. Sometimes chemicals and water is used to help lawns to grow. People have used grasses for a long time. People eat parts of grasses. Corn, wheat, barley, oats, rice and millet are cereals, common grains whose seeds are used for food and to make alcohol such as beer. Sugar comes from sugar cane, which is also a plant in the grass family. People have grown grasses as food for farm animals for about 4,000 years. People use bamboo to build houses, fences, furniture and other things. Grass plants can also be used as fuel, to cover roofs, and to weave baskets. n English, the word "grass" appears in several phrases. For example: "The grass is always greener on the other side" means "people are never happy with what they have and want something else." "Don't let the grass grow under your feet" means "Do something". "A snake in the grass" is about a person that will not be honest and will trick others. Grass is sometimes used as a slang term for cannabis (also called pot, weed, or marijuana) The Grass type (Japanese: くさタイプ Grass type) is one of the eighteen types. Prior to changes in Generation IV, all damaging Grass-type moves were special, but they may now also be physical depending on the attack. Grass-type Pokémon are immune to Leech Seed. Grass-type Pokémon are immune to Leech Seed Starting in Generation VI, Grass-type Pokémon are immune to powder and spore moves and Effect Spore.Grass types are tied with Rock in having the most weaknesses out of all types with five. Since Generation I, a particular asset of Grass types is being the only type that is immune to Leech Seed. As of Generation VI, Grass-type Pokémon are also immune to powder and spore moves, such as Sleep Powder and Stun Spore. Additionally, Grass Pokémon are the only ones affected by Rototiller and Flower Shield. Those moves raise both attack stats or the physical Defense stat, respectively, when used. Forest's Curse adds the Grass type to the target's types. Grass-type attacks are resisted by seven types, so they're tied with Bug as the most resisted type. Those resistant types are best covered by Rock and Ground. As of Generation VI, Dark and Ghost have neutral matchups against every type that resists Grass. When Grassy Terrain is in the effect, the power of Grass-type moves is increased by 30% (50% prior to Generation VIII) if the user is on the ground. Contest properties In contests, Grass-type moves are typically Clever moves, but can also be any of the other four contest conditions. As of Generation VIII, there are 112 Grass-type Pokémon or 12.27% of all Pokémon (counting those that are Grass-type in at least one of their forms), making it the third most common type after Normal and before Flying. A Pokémon with Protean or Libero will become a Grass-type Pokémon if it uses a Grass-type move. A Pokémon with Color Change, Imposter, Mimicry, RKS System, or Multitype will become a Grass-type Pokémon if (respectively) it is hit with a Grass-type move, is sent out against a Grass-type opponent, if the terrain is grassy, if it is holding a Grass Memory, or if it is holding a Meadow Plate or Grassium Z. Since Generation VI, Grass-type Pokémon are also immune to Effect Spore; Only Grass-type Pokémon can have these Abilities. This does not include signature Abilities.Due to the decreased amount of types in the TCG, Grass generally adopts all Bug-type Pokémon under its typing. It also adopted Poison-type Pokémon prior to the Diamond & Pearl set, after which they were moved to Psychic. Similar to the games, Grass-type Pokémon in the TCG are generally weak to Fire and resist Water. Grass-type Pokémon are strong against Fighting and Water Pokémon, whilst Metal Pokémon resisted it until the EX Power Keepers expansion set. Generation V introduced the most Grass-type Pokémon of any generation, with 21 (including Rotom's Mow form), and Generation VI introduced the fewest Grass-type Pokémon, with nine. Generation I introduced the most Grass-type moves of any generation, with 10, and Generation II introduced the fewest Grass-type moves, with three. The Grass type and/or Pokémon of the type have been referred to using the term "plant" instead on some occasions: In the English Generation I games, the Gym guide in Cerulean Gym refers to Pokémon of the Grass type as "plant Pokémon". In the English versions of Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen, he instead mentions "Grass-type Pokémon". In the Japanese versions of the Generation I games and FireRed and LeafGreen, he mentions the Grass type itself, calling it the "Plant type" (Japanese: しょくぶつタイプ). Another reference to "plant Pokémon" (Japanese: しょくぶつポケモン) is made by Professor Oak in the Japanese Pokémon Red, Green, and Blue, and international Pokémon Red and Blue, classifying Bulbasaur as such when the player is about to choose it as their starter. My interpretation of the theme: The theme starts as a predator waiting for its moment to strike (it feels familiar to void champion themes), then the chase begins followed by the act of a predator catching his prey (happens in rapid manor, pointing at how strong of a predator it is). From 0:50 it sounds like an ode to the predator, a marvellous tone in primeval world (possibly a reference to Brackern species as whole). At 1:51 there is a twist (the invasion of void and the fall of Brackern), it follows with uneasiness until 2:28 where whispers appeared (Skarner himself getting paranoid and conservative). 2:32, what once was an ode now transforms into nostalgic and melancholic composition of fallen majestic species and the last one of its kind consumed by fear and rage towards the threat that caused it all (the Void). 3:01, a reminder that Skarner is still that primeval being nobody should toy with (A sovereign of an Ixtal region).

It's important to understand that with this coming to LoL, one of the biggest games in the world, the interest for breaching and exploiting it is likely to grow. Also, no matter how much we enjoy League it is important to keep in mind that this is just a computer game. Is this level of intrusion really warranted for something like that? Riot games may not have other intentions, but someone else might in the future. I think steps like these lead to a dangerous philosophy where companies can arbitrairly decide on intrusive actions. Yes, I know a lot of data is being stored already but that does not mean that we should not be careful about how far we allow that to go. This is for sure a step in the wrong direction and laws should be made for this kind of stuff. Children are allowed to install LoL on their home computers, leaving the adults in the house completely unaware that there is a rootkit running in the background that in theory could be used to turn on your microphone, camera, read your keystrokes etc... 

While many games do use kernel level AC, at lest they run only when the game is on. And there have been incidents with these, such as the one with Genshin Impact. We need to draw a line for where the importance of fair play in video games comes in conflict with more important rights. Use it in tournaments and stuff, sure. But for everyone at all times? Thanks for taking the time to check out Hwei's theme! I'd like to extend a huge thank you to Riot Games for having me back to compose another Champion theme (although this one is obviously much different from Nilah's in pretty much every conceivable way). We worked really hard in order to create a theme that not only encapsulated Hwei's complex persona, but also told his tragic story. You may have already caught some of these details I’m about to share below if you've already listened at this point, but here are some general story bits that we tried to convey through the composition as well as the orchestration:

________

Solo Flute: Represents Hwei's "Light" (His kindness, vibrancy of mind and upbringing on Koyehn)

Solo Cello: Represents Hwei's "Darkness" (His dangerous intensity of expression and imagination as well as horrified intrigue and despair)

Piano: The connective tissue between the two (Also represents his more grounded, melancholic temperament)

Violin: Jhin/Jhin's influence

(0:00 - 1:12) - His early, peaceful life. Painting his visions for his temple masters.

(1:13 - 2:00) - As the years pass, he continues to paint according to the teachings of his temple (flute lead) while also venturing off on his own at night to paint his more "dangerous" and visionary art (cello joins).

(2:00) - Jhin....

(2:25 - 2:37) - Pleading conversation and confrontation with Jhin. This eventually leads to....

(3:03 - 3:43) - Present day Hwei, unshackled and wielding his art to fully express his complex visions in order to manipulate the world around him.

Love the little backstory we have for this group.
The misfits, troublemakers.
Guys who tried to make it big and lost, returned with bros by their side and at their back.
A second chance.

Sett the hard-worker who made what would be a career ending attack because of his anger management. Now he’s back as the boss with people who can rein him in and take it.

K’sante the big man with big dreams that outpaced his ability. He went big and lost trying to do it all. Now he has his posse to back him up where he falls short, rounding out his skills where now his big dreams seem reachable with such talented people.

Kayn the arrogant, attention-hogging, mentally unstable, edgy bad-boy loose cannon. But nonetheless driven, ambitious and skilled.
Following a bad breakup with his last band (Which let’s face it, was probably his fault) he’s determined to make a comeback with a crew that can match his ambitions and skills, but perhaps more importantly can also accept, tolerate, rein in or integrate his manic energy, giving him a productive outlet, and companions that have his back despite the cain he raises.

Ezreal the one-hit wonder, micromanaged into an abysmal pit following initial success. The least experienced but no less inspired and driven to hit stardom. Making a sense of himself with the freedom from his management he’s taken a risk on throwing his lot in with an assortment of driven artists, so crazy it might just work.
He’s still finding himself but brings his own unique energy to the group and with this team, he’s going to do great things.

Aphelios, the once hyper-talented singer cut tragically short by losing his voice. Finding a new direction with his creative vision and instrumental genius he puts together the boisterous mess into a coordinated chaos, giving them direction that lets their talents shine.
With this backup, he’s going to shoot for the moon again, down by circumstance, back with brothers.

And Yone, an eccentric artistic producer. Once a talented producer backing big names, but that was then. Disillusioned and disgusted with the monotony and uninspired corporate industry that music has become he left it behind.
But something about meeting these boys has lit that spark again. Determined to be different, make their mark as loudly and unashamedly themselves as possible, Yone sees in them what the industry lacks, and that’s why despite their antics and recklessness, it’s his honour to back these boys in their climb back up.

I’m back on board after T1 took their 6th championship—what a comeback!

This video is a honourary mention to an astonishing journey of the DRX sniper, Deft. Here is how it goes:
[0:09] Deft and Faker went to the same school, but only his friends know about how good Deft is; the rest only knows about Faker.
[0:42] The scene depicts while Deft are still deep in trouble (he joined MVP Blue but this team only got around the lower side of the league table), Faker had achieved his first glory ever; which can be seen as Deft used Ezreal to slain the Blue Sentinel, Faker as Zed slained the Baron (Faker won the first World Championship in 2013). MVP Blue and White then got bought by Samsung, eventually became SSW and SSB.
[0:58] PawN shot Deft as Jayce vs Lucian - in that respective World Championship, SSW PawN - eventually became world champions that year - had defeated SSB Deft. He left the team after the incident.
[1:12] Deft joined EDG with Meiko, and in his quest of the World Championship 2015, EDG lost 0 - 3 to FNC of Rekkles in the quarterfinals. Rekkles picked Kennen in the 1st game and did so incredible that EDG tried to reuse that pick but failed miserably.
[1:22] He joined KT in November 2016, and he was part of a "super team" at that time which won the LCK Summer 2018. However, in the World Championship 2018, KT lost to the eventual champions Invictus Gaming (iG) in an actually close battle from 0 - 2 to 2 - 2, and almost pulled the comeback off but the Urgot in game 5 backfired, and KT came out defeated. 
[1:55] Deft joined DRX, and the scene is from the year 2020 - Keria joins from the academy with Pyosik (Mark), and the GRF duo Doran and Chovy; but DRX was battered by the eventual world champions DWG (now DK) with a score of 0 - 3 in the quarterfinals. Graves by Canyon slained Doran as Jax; Keria was seen using Braum's E to tried blocking Showmaker's Syndra's R, but failed and Deft's Senna got the hold of Syndra's E. The sad thing is, during this time - Deft lost all three knockout encounters to DK (2 - 3 in Regional Finals 2019, 0 - 3 in both LCK Summer Grand Finals and Worlds 2020 Quarterfinals). 
He then joined HLE - but his LCK Spring run ended in 3rd, and the Summer one ended in 8th - but with the high coefficient they can still compete and they clinched the second seed but lost to T1 in the Regional Finals. As a result, in Worlds 2021 he had to start from Play-ins. The HLE team then got squashed by T1 in the Quarterfinals - again, with a 0 - 3 sweep.  
[2:05] He left HLE but then rejoined DRX the following season (which depicts in the vid that he fell into the a deep pit but then got rescued from the DRX teammates). This time, in the World Championship 2022, he must prepare himself. The emerging elevator could be a depiction of DRX going up from the Play-ins and the Group Stage, winning the tie-breaker to advance into the QF.
[2:25] He defeats Meiko (as Renata Glasc), an old teammate - indicating the reverse sweep of DRX against EDG in the quarterfinals.
[2:42] Deft as Varus shot Doran's Renekton, another old teammate. DRX defeated GEN 3-1 in the semifinals to face T1.
[2:50] Deft's Caitlyn got a face-off against Keria's Karma, who now plays for T1. Faker's Viktor came for the rescue, and almost killed Deft - but with Keria's Bard's E on-time,  his team came to the aid. Pyosik's Hecarim dives in first, then Kingen's Aatrox, and Deft's Caitlyn fires to finish it off. They finally won a World Championship and the dream became true. 
Deft became the oldest player ever to won Worlds, and DRX became the first team ever to win it as a Play-in round participant of the respective competition.

This is a great design. Each ability is easy enough to understand at face level, which is great, but using them well will be an interesting challenge. The bounce and knockback on his Q make it a simple ability with alot of depth, you could save it to interrupt channels from range, snub gank attempts, and harass enemies behind minions. The W allows for some interesting synergies with high-range ADCs, and managing its placement in a teamfight will be an important skill. The E is the simplest, but the charge system and ability to apply your passive will make who you choose to protect, and how much, an interesting dynamic. The ult is the ultimate choice. Do you use it to cleanse a crucial CC, or maximize the heal? Good players will make it do both. And of course, the passive is all-important. Good players will space out their abilities, both spatially and temporally, to maximize damage. 

All in all, a fantastic design, and a real breath of fresh air.

Edit: Coming back to see how this comment is doing; it’s inevitable and unfortunate how some are barking over Milio not being yet another over-the-top and edgy fantasy enchanter.
First, he is a fictional character. Characters are tools to further explore the story and their settings. True, Milio could've been just another edgy, masculine champ, but this was the direction chosen. You’ve already got *tons* of those archetypes within the game. Chill.
Secondly, you can be kind, brave, and strong regardless of identity. I’m glad to see the design and story of young male character reflect that in a support role (where the pool of most support champs is largely female character designs). I can even go as far as to also raise you other male support champs: Braum, Rakan, Pyke, even Alistar. 
At the end of the day, you're probably still playing League of Legends regardless lmao.

We need a reason to not give up. Give us rewards for mental fortitude so that people are encouraged to see things through rather than forfeit or throw the game.

"Jungle is wildly hard to learn" is a sentence that strikes fear into me for the sake of the complexity of the role actually staying intact- y'know with the whole nerfs to counter jungling and clearing two camps at once being more or less gone

The problem with the jungle role isn't that the jungle monsters are hard to kill, or that the leash range is too long (I genuinely do not know why they made leash ranges smaller and act like it's a good thing but another topic), the hard part about junge is being a babysitter for 4 other people who hate your guts and will find something to blame on you even if you literally play perfectly.  

You need to know timings, not only for camps and objectives but when and which lane to gank and why, which changes every game because of team compisition, how well a player is doing, everything. You need to know when to do a 3, 5 or 6 camp clear, when it's worth it to do objectives without making your team fall behind, when it's worth it to let the enemy do dragon/herald for other objectives, when it's more worth it to gank rather than farm or vice verse, all the while your team hates you for not ganking them 24/7. 

And the worst part is league communicates 0 of this information, there is no jungle tutorial and yes the jungle pets are cute, they solve nothing about the actual core problems of jungling.

I am a top main, but I have JG as my backup role and am good at it, and I like the *idea* of being the jungler a lot, but the reason I don't main jungle is because I don't want to spend every game getting flamed despite doing well because of the community's idea that them losing a 1v1 lane is the jungler's fault.

Based from observation these are his abilities: 

Passive - Every time he hits an ability against an enemy champion, his next auto attack deals bonus damage

Q - He slams the ground in short distance in front of him and slows all enemies hit. After hitting 2 Qs on enemy units, he can cast a third Q within a certain duration, that flings enemy champions to his back. 

W - He charges up a dash and travels a distance based on how long its charged up. He becomes CC immune while charging it up but cannot move nor use his other abilities while charging 

E - He dashes a short distance and gains a shield

R - He dashes a short distance towards a target direction and takes all enemies hit with him. If he uses this ability on an enemy champion against the wall, he takes them with him to the other side of the wall. He also instantly refills his mana bar but it slowly phases out after a certain duration.

Given the fact all his kills were under turrets his damage prolly not too overtuned. Kit look fun yet not too annoying to fight. K’Sante Passive Traveling Hunter.
K’Sante gains a new effect depending on where he is on the map. Changing locations on the map maintains the old effect along side the new effect for 5 seconds. If K’Sante is in the base, K’Sante gains a 5% Movement speed bonus. Apon leaving the base, heading toward the mid lane will gain K’Sante a shield that abosrbs magic damage equal to 10% of his maximum health and 20% of his missing health. If K’Sante kills an enemy champion while this shield holds up, K’Sante restores 15% of his missing health. If the shield is consumed, the shield exploses slowing all nearby enemies for 3 seconds. If K’Sante heads towards the top lane he will gain bonus armor equals to his minions & monsters kills score. Everytime K’Sante kills a minion while in the top lane, he also gains +1 attack damage until he leaves to another area of the map. If K’Sante kills an enemy champion while in the top lane, he loses this bonus attack damage and converts it to gold instead. If K’Sante enters the jungle he gains Track Monsters, allwing him to sense the presence of enemy champions and monsters in the jungle while out of combat. If K’Sante enters combat while in the jungle he loses Track Monsters and gain Kill Monsters instead, increasing his attack speed by 2% everytime he autoattacks. He K’Sante kills a monster in the jungle before reaching 10% bonuce attack speed, he gains a permanent 1% attack speed. If K’Sante enters the bottom lane he gains a shield that absorbs physical damage equal to 50% of all allies in the bottom lane's missing health. This shield refreshes after entering and leaving combat with enemy champions. If K’Sante enters the enemy base, he gains the effects of all other zones combined for 10 seconds. Apon leaving the enemy base K’Sante cannot benefit from any zone bonuses for the next 15 seconds. However after those 15 seconds the next bonus gained will be doubled for the first 5 seconds, unless K’Sante enters combat with an enemy champion, in this case the bonus will be doubled for 7 seconds.

I've been playing this game for 6+ years on and off, but every time I invest any serious amount of time, my mental health suffers greatly-- a lot of this has to due with long grind this game promotes via ranked(used to be much shorter before the "mmr" changes), the overwhelming amount of low quality games that are infuriating, and the very "rigged" feel of matchmaking.

You will end up feeling sour about all the time you wasted in something so inherently toxic, so dubious and grindy by nature. It will make your life worse if you invest any serious time into it. 

I don't know what it is, but it definitely feels as if ranked is rigged to force you into a 50% winrate so it takes forever for you to climb, promoting you to stay playing the game longer. You can't escape this manipulated matchmaking even in normals-- check out my normal games under IGN: LOL Rigged Game. The moment I hard win 2-3 games, I'm given extremely toxic teammates that don't know what they're doing, int, and/or AFK. It will be like this for multiple games. Now instead of me naturally just winning the games if the matchmaking was unmanipulated, I'm forced to play more games to get to lvl 30 since losing = less exp.

The more infuriating part is that because my "mmr" is high, my queue times are very long-- like 10+ mins-- so it adds to more time wasted before a pretty infuriating loss.

I feel, even after getting Diamond multiple times and investing a lot of time improving, that no matter what I do, I cannot beat the matchmaking system. I can try my hardest, absolute best, but I feel that I cannot control the outcome in most of my games no matter what game mode it is. The matchmaking feels like the strongest factor, not myself. 

League will do nothing but make your life worse-- be ware!

My mental health was already on thin ice before the we received the terrible news so my family decided that it'd be better for me not to attend, but they said i could if i wanted to, yet i didn't. I hate myself for that moment of weakness. I couldn't say my final goodbye to him. Since he passed away i rarely visited his grave, i just couldn't. I'd start hyperventilating and having a panic attack. Two and a half weeks ago i moved abroad, 1200 km away to be exact and i didn't visit his grave even though I planned that for months if i were to ever move away, but when it actually came to me moving, it literally happened from one day to the other. 
The lines:
"Someday I’ll bе overcast, but you won't have to cry
’Cause wе'll do the grieving, while I'm by your side"
remind me so much of him. This is something that he would've said.

For anyone wondering or don't know, the music is based off of South Indian Hindu style of music. And the Vocals are a Hindu Southern Indian Style of singing. It's basically like the western "Do Re Mi Fa So La Ti Do", but in India, we have our own version of it, in which we instead say "Sa Ri Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa". And in the Indian style of singing, we sing it fast and with "trippy" rhythm. And as for Nilah herself, her whip seems inspired by a real-life southern Indian blade called an "Urumi", in which it's basically a giant blade, but acts like a killer whip, making it very difficult to master and is taught last, since it can chop multiple heads at once, as well as your own. And it can come with multiple blades in one handle even. Nilah's design even seems to be based off a female South Indian Warrior.

EDIT: I love all y'alls input, but I'm a silver player. While ADCs do have multiple things to survive nowadays, answers like "oh you have your support" or "you are supposed to be glass cannons" are not really helping or constructive in anyway.
1. Most supports are trash in this elo. Maybe every 5th support I have is actually useful and doesn't just feed, blame me for everything going wrong (and in conclusion tilting) or leave my lane lvl 2 so I would die.
2. I'm everything but a perfect player. I missplay a lot and have to take that into account when playing against champions with this many dashes. A single mistake on my part will lead to my death, while a mistake on the enemy's part doesn't have any impact considering I have no chance to run while they can dash 3x to get to me.
3. No, I don't play champions with dashes (except Caitlyn). Champions like Samira, Akshan, Zeri, Vayne etc are not part of my repertoire - I don't enjoy playing them too much and will not bother learning to play them just because Riot thinks that dashes are a key element to every kit nowadays.
4. Flash and Galeforce are not enough to get me away from champs with hypermobility. I don't play heal either, I play exhaust for the 1on1 potential. And considering the recent Galeforce nerf, I've been playing Kraken Slayer way more recently. The item choices for Jinx mains aren't too customizable when it comes to survivability or actually dealing damage.

So again, thanks for y'alls opinions, but not everyone is actually a high elo player. I enjoy having fun in the game and considering how weak ADCs are in lower elo (when you take all the other champions like Xin Zhao, Fiora, Irelia etc. in account), it's not enjoyable or any kind of fun. Adding champions is great and all, but every kit nowadays is so extremely overloaded. I love the fact that this theme (excluding the eerie intro and outro) is like the background music of perfume commercials, given that her character mostly revolves around chemicals, hence her epithet.

And also, despite some earlier comments that I saw saying that they didn't like this theme because it is more different than the champion trailer due to the missing "madness" part, I still like this theme more than that since I believe that if the trailer music focuses more on her madness in the outside, this final theme focuses more on what she feels in the inside. Yes, we can feel the elegance, danger, and superiority in this theme like in the trailer, but this time, it is more sad when it comes to its tunes. I agree that the intense part of this theme is not as "intense" as expected just like what the other comments stated, since we can still feel that lingering sense of a somewhat "hidden" grief. This  suggests that more than the madness she is about to unleash in a snap of her fingers, her reputation and strong personality as a dangerous, strong, independent lady/businesswoman/political figure from Zaun, deep inside, she is still that little girl grieving the loss of her parents and is therefore attempting to seek revenge and justice in an unjust world where if you are poor, despite helping many people, you are voiceless.
